statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Prove that the incircles of triangles $ABC$, $BCD$, $CDA$, and $DAB$ have a common point if and only if $ABCD$ is a rhombus.
Determine all values of $n$ such that it is possible to divide a triangle into $n$ smaller triangles with no three collinear vertices and such that each vertex belongs to the same number of segments.
Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2004}$ be a sequence of integers such that $x_{k+3} = x_{k+2} + x_k x_{k+1}$ for all $1 \leq k \leq 2001$. Is it possible that more than half of the elements are negative?

Consider all ways of writing each of the numbers $0, 1, 2, \ldots, 9$ exactly ten times in the squares of a $10 \times 10$ board. Find the greatest integer $n$ with the property that there is always a row or a column containing at least $n$ different numbers.
Consider the sequence $(a_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $a_0 = a_1 = a_2 = a_3 = 1$ and $a_n a_{n-4} = a_{n-1}a_{n-3} + a_{n-2}^2$. Prove that all terms of the sequence are integers.

Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Define $f_{a,b} : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ by $f_{a,b}(x,y) = (a - by - x^2,\, x)$. The set $\mathrm{per}(a,b)$ of periodic points of $f_{a,b}$ consists of all $P \in \mathbb{R}^2$ such that $f_{a,b}^n(P) = P$ for some positive integer $n$. Fix $b$. Prove that the set $A_b = \{a \in \mathbb{R} \mid \mathrm{per}(a,b) \neq \emptyset\}$ has a minimum, and find this minimum.
